Copernicus Emergency Management Service Maps Flood Damages in Northern Nepal

2026-08-28 EU Space Support Office Copernicus, CEMS, emergency mapping, flood, Nepal, Tibet, glacier collapse, satellite imagery, disaster response
Read the source article

Quick summary

The Copernicus Emergency Management Service activated its Rapid Mapping component to assess flood damage in northern Nepal after a glacier collapse triggered a devastating debris avalanche and flash flood on August 26, 2026.

Key takeaways

  • A high-altitude glacier partially collapsed on August 26, 2026, triggering an ice and rock avalanche that descended 1,200 metres into the Lhende River basin
  • The Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS) activated Rapid Mapping under activation EMSR927 to map flood extent and assess damage across four Areas of Interest
  • CEMS analysis around the village of Syapru Besi identified more than 240 buildings destroyed and 32 damaged
  • The event affected northern Nepal and Tibet, generating powerful flows of water, mud, and debris downstream
  • The satellite-derived damage maps support emergency response and recovery planning
